actuator_details: Visual-inertial SLAM library. ORB feature extraction + bag-of-words place recognition + bundle adjustment over keyframes. Supports monocular, stereo, RGB-D, and visual-inertial sensor configurations. Multi-map operation with map-merging. Real-time on commodity CPU.
control_architecture: Provides SLAM substrate for any robotic platform with a camera. C++ library; ROS 1/2 integration.
creator: University of Zaragoza I3A; Carlos Campos, Juan Tardós et al.
disclosure_citation: Campos, C., Elvira, R., Rodríguez, J. J. G., Montiel, J. M. M., Tardós, J. D. 'ORB-SLAM3: An Accurate Open-Source Library for Visual, Visual-Inertial, and Multimap SLAM'. IEEE Transactions on Robotics 37(6) December 2021, pp. 1874-1890. arXiv:2007.11898. GPLv3 source: github.com/UZ-SLAMLab/ORB_SLAM3. University of Zaragoza.
notable_capabilities: the canonical visual-inertial SLAM baseline since 2021
deployed in countless academic + commercial robotic systems
prior_art_notes: ORB-SLAM3 is the canonical academic visual-inertial SLAM library and 5-year-deep open-source baseline. Heavily-cited (>3000 citations). Anticipates: (1) monocular/stereo/RGB-D + IMU fusion in a unified factor-graph framework, (2) multi-map operation across sessions for long-term autonomy, (3) bag-of-words place recognition for loop closure. Establishes the geometric-only SLAM baseline that semantic/open-vocab SLAM systems (including RADIO-ViPE, round-10 entry) extend. Any humanoid platform claim on visual-inertial SLAM faces this lineage.
sources: Campos et al. IEEE T-RO 37(6) 2021.
ORB-SLAM3 GitHub (github.com/UZ-SLAMLab/ORB_SLAM3) GPLv3.
ORB-SLAM lineage: Mur-Artal/Tardós ORB-SLAM (2015), ORB-SLAM2 (2017).

actuator_details: End-to-end differentiable visual SLAM. Dense bundle adjustment over all pixels (vs. ORB-SLAM's sparse keypoint approach). Recurrent iterative optical-flow updates produce dense correspondences and depth. GPU-accelerated. Significantly more robust to texture-poor scenes and dynamic content than ORB-SLAM3.
control_architecture: Visual SLAM substrate. PyTorch implementation; supports monocular/stereo/RGB-D inputs.
creator: Princeton Vision and Learning Lab; Zachary Teed, Jia Deng
disclosure_citation: Teed, Z., Deng, J. 'DROID-SLAM: Deep Visual SLAM for Monocular, Stereo, and RGB-D Cameras'. NeurIPS 2021. arXiv:2108.10869. BSD-3-Clause source: github.com/princeton-vl/DROID-SLAM. Princeton Vision and Learning Lab.
notable_capabilities: robust to texture-poor and dynamic scenes
the foundation for ViPE and downstream semantic SLAM systems
prior_art_notes: DROID-SLAM is the canonical dense differentiable-visual-SLAM academic system (NeurIPS 2021, BSD-3 open source). 4-year-deep prior art anticipating any humanoid claim on dense / differentiable / foundation-model-grounded visual SLAM. Immediate ancestor of ViPE (Princeton 2024-2025) and RADIO-ViPE (ITMO 2026 — round-10 entry). Together with ORB-SLAM3, establishes the academic SLAM baseline against which all modern humanoid perception claims must be evaluated.
sources: Teed, Z., Deng, J. NeurIPS 2021.
DROID-SLAM GitHub (github.com/princeton-vl/DROID-SLAM) BSD-3-Clause.
Predecessor: RAFT (Teed/Deng ECCV 2020) for optical flow.

actuator_details: Online semantic SLAM system. Calibration-free monocular RGB input — no prior camera intrinsics, no depth, no pose initialization required. Tightly couples multi-modal embeddings (RADIO agglomerative foundation model + SigLIP text encoder) with geometric scene information in a joint factor-graph optimization with adaptive robust kernels. Operates online at 8-10 FPS. State-of-the-art on TUM-RGBD dynamic benchmark (ATE 1.63 cm average vs. ViPE 2.17 / Dyna-SLAM 2.00).
aliases: Reduce All Domains Into One Video Pose Engine
control_architecture: Provides perception substrate for any robot with a camera. Outputs: calibrated camera poses, dense depth maps, dense PCA-compressed RADIO embeddings per pixel. Supports free-form natural-language object queries via SigLIP text-embedding matching against the dense map. Three-regime Barron-loss adaptive robust kernel jointly suppresses actively-moving agents and quasi-static displaced objects.
creator: ITMO University BE2R Lab; Nasser, Iumanov, Li, Popov, Mahmoud, Kolyubin
disclosure_citation: Nasser, Z., Iumanov, M., Li, T., Popov, M., Mahmoud, J., Kolyubin, S. 'RADIO-ViPE: Online Tightly Coupled Multi-Modal Fusion for Open-Vocabulary Semantic SLAM in Dynamic Environments'. arXiv:2604.26067v1, April 28, 2026. ITMO University, Biomechatronics and Energy-Efficient Robotics (BE2R) Lab, Saint Petersburg, Russia.
notable_capabilities: calibration-free (no camera intrinsics, no depth, no pose required)
SOTA on TUM-RGBD dynamic benchmark (ATE 1.63 cm)
prior_art_notes: RADIO-ViPE is the most recent and architecturally complete online open-vocabulary semantic SLAM system. April 2026 arXiv preprint; 9 days before this corpus entry. Establishes very-recent (sub-1-week) open-academic prior art for: calibration-free monocular semantic SLAM, tightly-coupled multi-modal fusion (RADIO + SigLIP + geometric BA), adaptive-kernel dynamic-scene robustness, online operation at 8-10 FPS. Directly shields any commercial humanoid claim on: 'onboard semantic scene understanding from monocular video' (Tesla Optimus, Figure 02, 1X NEO, Apptronik Apollo, etc. all face this), 'language-grounded robotic perception in dynamic environments', 'calibration-free humanoid camera deployment'. The TUM-RGBD ATE comparison table in Table II of the paper enumerates the prior art — RADIO-ViPE outperforms Dyna-SLAM, DLD-SLAM, V3D-SLAM, DGS-SLAM, RoDyn-SLAM, DynaMON, ViPE — every one of which is itself open-academic prior art for humanoid perception. Lineage: ORB-SLAM3 (geometric baseline) → DROID-SLAM (dense differentiable) → ViPE (Princeton in-the-wild metric depth) → RADIO-ViPE (ITMO open-vocab + calibration-free).
sensing: single uncalibrated monocular RGB camera (the entire input); produces depth + pose + dense semantic embeddings as output
sources: Nasser et al. arXiv:2604.26067v1 April 2026.
ITMO BE2R Lab (itmo.ru/en/faculties_and_institutes/96/).

Foundation models: NVIDIA RADIO (Ranzinger et al. 2024), SigLIP (Zhai et al. ICCV 2023).

actuator_details: Mid-scale humanoid (~1.4 m, ~30 kg target class). In-house-built lightweight design optimized for learning-based control: low simulation complexity, anthropomorphic kinematics, and reliability against falls. Quasi-direct-drive actuators in legs and arms. Specific motor/reducer selection in the public arXiv paper.
control_architecture: Reinforcement-learning locomotion controller trained in simulation with light domain randomization; deployed zero-shot to hardware. Demonstrates narrow sim-to-real gap and robust locomotion across outdoor terrains. The platform is explicitly designed as a research substrate for learning-based control rather than a closed product.

disclosure_citation: Liao, Q., Zhang, B., Huang, X., Huang, X., Li, Z., Sreenath, K. 'Berkeley Humanoid: A Research Platform for Learning-based Control'. arXiv:2407.21781, July 2024. IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA) 2025. UC Berkeley Hybrid Robotics Lab.
notable_capabilities: outdoor robust bipedal locomotion (hundreds of meters)
RL controller with zero-shot sim-to-real deployment
open-source via UC Berkeley Hybrid Robotics Lab

Establishes 1-year-deep prior art for: RL-trained locomotion with sim-to-real zero-shot transfer at humanoid scale, low-cost in-house-built humanoid for learning research, anthropomorphic kinematics optimized for sim-to-real. Direct shielding for free-humanoid-platform commitments on bipedal RL locomotion and any commercial humanoid claim on RL-trained outdoor walking. actuator_details: Sub-$5,000 open-source 3D-printed humanoid. ~0.8 m tall, ~16 kg. **3D-printed cycloidal-gear actuators** — the design choice that makes the BOM accessible — paired with widely-available off-the-shelf brushless motors. Modular gearbox replaceable per finger / joint. The design explicitly trades absolute durability for reproducibility and democratization.
control_architecture: RL-trained locomotion controller; zero-shot sim-to-real demonstrated. Hardware design + embedded code + training/deployment frameworks all fully open-source. Designed for researchers, students, and tech newbies — explicitly democratization-oriented.

actuator_details: Compact (~0.56 m, 3.4 kg) anthropomorphic humanoid with 30 active DoF (excluding end effectors). Commercially available off-the-shelf motors; entirely 3D-printed. Total BOM under $6,000. Plug-and-play zero-point calibration and transferable motor system identification for sim-to-real.
control_architecture: Designed as ML-compatible substrate. High-fidelity digital twin via system-ID; demonstrated zero-shot sim-to-real policy transfer for both locomotion and manipulation. Loco-manipulation tasks in the demonstration set.

Establishes 1-year-deep open-academic prior art for: integrated loco-manipulation policy training on an open humanoid platform, transferable motor system-ID for sim-to-real without hand-tuning, 30-DoF anthropomorphic full-body at sub-$6k. actuator_details: Online video pose engine: from raw uncalibrated video, estimates camera intrinsics, camera motion (poses), and dense near-metric depth maps. Supports pinhole, wide-angle, and 360° panoramic camera models. Solves a dense bundle adjustment with multi-constraint loss. Runs at 3-5 FPS on a single GPU. Outperforms MegaSAM and prior uncalibrated baselines by 18% / 50% on TUM / KITTI benchmarks.
control_architecture: Provides perception substrate (intrinsics + extrinsics + dense depth) for any robotic platform with monocular video. Released with a 96M-frame dataset of paired video + camera-pose + dense-depth annotations across internet videos, AI-generated videos, and panoramas — the largest such open dataset to date.
creator: NVIDIA Toronto AI Lab (nv-tlabs); multi-author
disclosure_citation: Huang, J., et al. (NVIDIA Toronto AI Lab + collaborators). 'ViPE: Video Pose Engine for 3D Geometric Perception'. arXiv:2508.10934, August 2025. Open-source release via nv-tlabs/vipe.
notable_capabilities: calibration-free metric depth and pose from unconstrained video
support for pinhole, wide-angle, and 360° cameras

prior_art_notes: ViPE is NVIDIA Toronto AI Lab's canonical Video Pose Engine, August 2025 arXiv. Sits **directly between DROID-SLAM (2021) and RADIO-ViPE (2026)** in the visual-SLAM lineage: it is RADIO-ViPE's explicit foundation per the round-10 paper's text ('we build upon ViPE [5]'). 9-month-deep open-permissive academic prior art for: calibration-free metric depth from uncalibrated video, dense bundle adjustment over heterogeneous camera models, online video pose estimation at 3-5 FPS. Direct shielding for any commercial humanoid claim on uncalibrated-camera onboard 3D perception. Plus the 96M-frame released dataset is itself prior art for any humanoid-vision data-curation IP.

actuator_details: Monocular Gaussian-splatting SLAM specifically engineered for dynamic-scene robustness. Tracks camera trajectory and reconstructs a 3D Gaussian map of the static environment from monocular video, even with dynamic distractors (people, moving objects). Renders high-fidelity novel views of the static scene from the trained Gaussian field.

Establishes 1-year-deep prior art for: monocular GS-SLAM with dynamic-scene robustness, photorealistic novel-view rendering of static background while filtering dynamic foreground. actuator_details: Real-time whole-body model-predictive controller using MuJoCo dynamics directly. Iterative LQR (iLQR) optimization with finite-difference approximation of dynamics derivatives — no analytical model required. Achieves real-time on hardware for: dynamic quadruped locomotion, quadruped walking on two legs, and full-sized humanoid bipedal locomotion.

direct extension of the Tassa iLQG (2012) lineage

actuator_details: Five-finger 3D-printed anthropomorphic hand. **Antagonistic-tendon mechanism** — agonist + antagonist tendon pairs allow active opening AND closing (classic SoftHand only actively closes; passive return). Two-layer palm design with separate routing for agonist vs. antagonist tendons. Two differential mechanisms enable distinct joint control modes: enclosing grasp vs. fingertip grasp.
control_architecture: Highly underactuated — synergy-driven from a small number of motors (specific count in paper). Tactile feedback via integrated vision-based tactile sensors at fingertips. Dual-tendon active control allows specific joint targeting (DIP vs. PIP).

actuator_details: Vision-language-action **flow model** for general robot control. Pretrained on diverse multi-robot demonstration data (mobile manipulation, bimanual, single-arm). Single foundation policy controls multiple robot embodiments. Action distribution modeled via flow matching (vs. diffusion or autoregressive). Significant step in unified-VLA-foundation-model lineage post RT-2 / OpenVLA.

Hybrid multi-modal examples combine image observations + language commands + object detections + semantic-subtask prediction + low-level actions. actuator_details: Optimized fine-tuning recipe for VLA models, applied to OpenVLA as base. Combines: (1) parallel decoding of action tokens, (2) action chunking, (3) continuous action representation (vs. discretized), (4) L1 regression-based learning objective. Improves OpenVLA average success on LIBERO from 76.5% → 97.1% and increases action throughput by 26×. Real-world bimanual ALOHA evaluations beat π₀ and RDT-1B fine-tuned defaults plus from-scratch Diffusion Policy and ACT by up to 15% absolute success rate.
control_architecture: Fine-tuning recipe for VLA foundation models. Publishes the speed × success Pareto improvement.
creator: Stanford; Moo Jin Kim, Chelsea Finn, Percy Liang

outperforms π₀ + RDT-1B + Diffusion Policy + ACT on bimanual ALOHA
prior_art_notes: OpenVLA-OFT is the canonical Optimized Fine-Tuning recipe for VLA models (Stanford, Feb 2025). 15-month-deep prior art on: parallel action decoding for VLA, action chunking + continuous action representation + L1 regression objective combination. Direct shielding for any commercial humanoid VLA fine-tuning claim, particularly any claim on 'fast inference at high success' for humanoid VLAs. Outperforms π₀ on bimanual ALOHA — the canonical academic benchmark for bimanual humanoid manipulation.

actuator_details: Anthropomorphic robot hand built **entirely from LEGO MINDSTORMS** components and standard LEGO bricks. Tendon-driven highly-underactuated five-finger hand based on the Pisa-IIT SoftHand and Tactile SoftHand-A lineage. **Dual motors driving an agonist-antagonist tendon pair on each finger** for active fine control. Finger motions synchronized via **soft synergies implemented with a differential mechanism using clutch gears** (a LEGO-friendly approximation of the SoftHand's textile-elastic synergies). 90% of the grip force of a professional 3D-printed SoftHand. <1 second open-close cycle.
control_architecture: LEGO MINDSTORMS hub controls dual motors per finger via standard LEGO interfaces. Designed for educational replication — full open-source build instructions and CAD files at lepora.com/EduSoftHand-A. Programmable via standard MINDSTORMS environment.

disclosure_citation: Lepora, J., Li, H., Psomopoulou, E., Lepora, N. F. 'Educational SoftHand-A: Building an Anthropomorphic Hand with Soft Synergies using LEGO® MINDSTORMS®'. arXiv:2510.15638, October 2025. Bristol Robotics Laboratory + Bristol Grammar School.
end_effector: five LEGO-built fingers with antagonistic tendons; differential clutch-gear synergy
notable_capabilities: anthropomorphic 5-finger hand from LEGO MINDSTORMS only

prior_art_notes: Educational SoftHand-A is the LEGO MINDSTORMS instantiation of the Pisa-IIT SoftHand / Tactile SoftHand-A lineage (Oct 2025). 7-month-deep prior art for: differential clutch-gear synergy mechanism in LEGO bricks, agonist-antagonist tendon pair from a single dual-motor module, accessible educational reproduction of professional SoftHand-class designs. **Direct relevance for free-humanoid-platform hand v0.2** — the differential-synergy clutch-gear approach is documented open art that the v0.2 hand could adopt or explicitly diverge from. Together with pisa-iit-softhand, pisa-iit-softhand-2, and tactile-softhand-a-2025, the SoftHand synergy-mechanism lineage is now 11-year-deep continuous open academic publication (2014-2025) across four design generations.

actuator_details: Open-source middleware for robotics. Publish-subscribe message-passing architecture, packaged build system, large set of community-contributed drivers and algorithm packages. Becomes the de facto integration substrate for academic and commercial robots through the 2010s.
control_architecture: Provides communication, build, and tooling substrate for arbitrary robotic systems. Per-platform drivers; perception/navigation/manipulation algorithm packages.

Lifecycle-managed nodes, native security, deterministic execution. The substrate for modern academic + commercial robotics integration.

actuator_details: Physics simulation engine optimized for model-based control: stable contact dynamics, fast forward + inverse dynamics, smooth analytical derivatives. Designed expressly for the iLQG / MPC use case (Tassa iLQG 2012 entry uses MuJoCo). The dominant academic simulator for humanoid and manipulator policy training since the mid-2010s.
control_architecture: Provides simulation substrate for arbitrary control architectures. Standard MJCF model format; Python (mujoco) and C bindings.
creator: Emo Todorov, Tom Erez, Yuval Tassa (originally University of Washington / Roboti LLC; now Google DeepMind)
disclosure_citation: Todorov, E., Erez, T., Tassa, Y. 'MuJoCo: A physics engine for model-based control'. IROS 2012. Originally proprietary (Roboti LLC); acquired by Google DeepMind October 2021 and released under Apache-2.0.

The substrate that the Tassa iLQG entry, Howell-Tassa MuJoCo MPC entry, MJX entry, and Genesis simulator entry all build on or interop with. Direct shielding for any commercial humanoid claim on contact-rich policy training simulation. MJCF is the format OpenLoco compiles to, so MuJoCo is the reference simulator for the entire free-humanoid-family.

actuator_details: Model-based design + verification toolkit for robotics. Multibody dynamics + collision + contact + linear/nonlinear systems theory + MPC + LCP/QP solvers in a unified C++/Python framework. Strong emphasis on formal verification and deterministic semantics — the feature distinguishing Drake from MuJoCo. Used at MIT, TRI, Boston Dynamics, and across academia.
control_architecture: Multibody dynamics + systems framework + optimization-based control toolkit. Provides MPC / TVLQR / QP-based whole-body control templates.
creator: MIT CSAIL Robot Locomotion Group + Toyota Research Institute; Russ Tedrake et al.

Direct shielding for any commercial humanoid claim on verifiable model-based control or whole-body QP/MPC architectures. actuator_details: GPU-parallelized physics simulator for robotic RL. End-to-end GPU pipeline: simulation, observation extraction, neural network inference, policy update — no CPU round-trip. Enables thousands of parallel environment instances on a single GPU. The substrate for ANYmal sim-to-real perceptive locomotion (Hwangbo 2019 → Lee 2020 → Miki 2022 lineage).

actuator_details: Vision foundation model trained by **agglomerative multi-teacher distillation** from CLIP, DINOv2, and SAM. Single backbone inheriting all three teacher capabilities: zero-shot vision-language, dense pixel-level features, open-vocabulary segmentation. Released across multiple sizes (RADIO-B/L/H). Used as the perception substrate for RADIO-ViPE (round-10 entry) and other downstream robotics systems.

The default vision-language encoder for many modern VLAs (e.g., OpenVLA uses SigLIP + DINOv2).

actuator_details: Transformer-based diffusion-policy generalist robot policy. Trained on **800k robot trajectories** from a curated 25-dataset subset of the Open X-Embodiment dataset. Two model sizes: Octo-Small (27M parameters) and Octo-Base (93M parameters). Open weights, open code, open dataset. Demonstrated zero-shot and few-shot transfer across 9 robotic platforms with new observation and action spaces.
control_architecture: Transformer + diffusion-policy action head. Conditioned on language instruction OR goal image. Lightweight finetuning recipe enables adaptation to new robots in hours on consumer GPUs.

actuator_details: **Vision-Language-Action foundation model purpose-built for humanoid robots.** Dual-system architecture inspired by human cognition: System 1 fast-thinking action model (reflex-class); System 2 slow-thinking deliberate-decision model. 2B parameters in the public N1 release. Trained on a diverse mix: **egocentric human videos + real robot trajectories + simulated robot trajectories + synthetic data**. The N1.7 successor adds Cosmos-Reason2-2B VLM backbone + 20,854-hour EgoScale pre-training across 20+ task categories.
control_architecture: Dual-system VLA: S2 internet-pretrained reasoning model + S1 fast reactive policy. Direct architectural lineage with Figure Helix's S1/S2 design (round-15 entry below). Generalizes across grasping, moving objects with one or both arms, and multi-step long-context tasks.

actuator_details: **Dual-system VLA** for humanoid upper-body control. **System 2 (S2)** — onboard internet-pretrained VLM at 7-9 Hz for scene understanding + language comprehension. **System 1 (S1)** — fast reactive visuomotor policy at 200 Hz translating S2's latent semantic representations into precise continuous actions. **35-DoF action space** at 200 Hz: individual fingers + end-effector + head gaze + torso. Single weight set across all behaviors. Trained on ~500 hours of multi-robot multi-operator teleoperated data with auto-labeling VLM hindsight instructions. Runs **entirely onboard embedded low-power GPUs**.
control_architecture: S1/S2 dual-system architecture. Direct architectural sibling of NVIDIA GR00T N1 (round-15 entry above) — both released within weeks of each other; both adopt the cognitive-science S1/S2 pattern. Helix's distinguishing claim: 200 Hz continuous control of full upper body (35 DoF including individual fingers + torso + head + wrists) — finer-grain action space than RT-2 / OpenVLA / π₀'s coarser end-effector trajectories. Multi-robot collaboration demonstrated (two humanoids cooperating on shared task).

prior_art_notes: Helix is Figure AI's canonical 2025 commercial humanoid VLA. Public-disclosure surface (corporate blog + demo videos + Hacker News + Robot Report coverage) reveals architecture (S1/S2 dual-system, 35-DoF/200Hz, ~500hr teleop training) but withholds neural-network specifics, training-data composition, fine-tuning recipe, and policy-evaluation metrics. The capability set claimed is fully covered by deep open academic prior art chains: (1) S1/S2 dual-system architecture is shared with NVIDIA GR00T N1 (round-15 entry, released within weeks; the cognitive-science S1/S2 pattern dates to Kahneman 'Thinking Fast and Slow' 2011); (2) high-rate continuous VLA control was demonstrated by π₀ (round-12, October 2024) and π₀.₅ (round-12, April 2025) in diffusion/flow-matching form; (3) onboard low-power VLA inference is anticipated by OpenVLA-OFT (round-12, parallel decoding + 26× throughput); (4) multi-robot collaboration is anticipated by ROS 2 (round-13, real-time multi-vehicle middleware) and the Mobile ALOHA / ACT bimanual lineage. Direct shielding for any Helix or Helix-derivative commercial-IP claim.

The full Optimus Gen 3 claim surface is therefore element-by-element anticipated by deep open academic chains plus prior commercial humanoids in the corpus.
